subject: Sharing Plot On Several Pages in a Shiny App

messages.author: de0353bdfec15530
messages.subject: Sharing Plot On Several Pages in a Shiny App
parts:
Hi all,

I have an app using a navbarPage layout consisting of several tabPanels.  What I'd like to do in server.R is have a single renderPlot call (to limit code duplication) that creates a plot, but then the plot is displayed on several tabPanels (by referring to the appropriate outpitId twice in ui.R).  I've tried doing this, but then when I load the app, neither plot loads, and in fact a bunch of other functionality breaks.  I seem to remember reading somewhere that I should be able to refer to the same outputId more than once in ui.R -- does anyone know if this is the case, or is the problem specific to my app?

If the problem is specific to my app then I'll try creating a reproducible example if I have the time.

Thanks!

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Sharing Plot On Several Pages in a Shiny App
parts:
You can't refer to the same outputId more than once, it won't work and will raise an error in your JavaScript console.

I wouldn't worry about the code duplication of renderPlot--just make a function:

makePlot <- function() {
  renderPlot({ ... })
}

output$plot_tab1 <- makePlot()
output$plot_tab2 <- makePlot()
output$plot_tab3 <- makePlot()

The unfortunate thing about this approach is not code duplication, but the fact that as you navigate between tabs the plot will actually have to be plotted once per tab, which is unfortunate.

Depending on your layout, you might be able to use navbarPage's header and footer arguments to put the plot on the page just once, outside of the area that the navbar affects.
